title: I want you to fix this.
body:
This is an amazing app, and I use it every day. However, there’s one thing I’d really like to see improved.

When I want to type something like “1-4pm” in the title of an event, the app automatically interprets it as a date and time.

For example, if I enter:
“1-4pm rehearsal”

the app treats “1-4” as January 4, and “4pm” is removed from the title and used as the event time instead.

I don’t want the app to interpret what I type—I just want the text to stay exactly as I entered it. Later, when I look for the event, I end up thinking, “I could have sworn I created it,” because it was changed automatically.

The automatic date and time recognition can be useful, but I’d really appreciate having an option to turn it off, or at least keep the text exactly as typed instead of modifying it automatically.
developer_response:
Thank you for your support of TickTick and for providing such a detailed explanation.
To manage how dates are handled, you can use the following methods:

1、Cancel Recognition for a Single Task: If a date or time is automatically highlighted while typing, you can click on the recognized text or press the Backspace key to cancel the recognition for that instance. Please note that this will also prevent the task time from being automatically set.

2、Keep Date Text in Titles Globally: If you want TickTick to recognize the time but keep the original words in the title, please go to Settings → More Settings → Smart Recognition and disable the "Remove Date from Text" option. Once disabled, phrases like "rehearsal from 1 PM to 4 PM" will be automatically recognized as a time duration while remaining exactly as typed in your task title.
We hope this information helps!

title: Fantastic except for one confusing problem…
body:
More user friendly than Todoist- also looks better because of recent updates. I think it is the best to do list all that exists. Full stop. And I’ve tried way too many.

The only problem it has: I use the date property in my tasks to mark their deadlines, if they have deadlines- when they’ve got to be done by. I usually try to complete those tasks long before the deadline comes. How should I use the calendar feature in TickTick to schedule my tasks with time blocking? If I put them on my calendar for when I will do them, then the date property no longer represents the deadline for the task. So, I simply can’t use the calendar for time blocking. Isn’t that supposed to be the main purpose of having a calendar inside TickTick? Unfortunate. 

Adding a separate date property called “deadline“ would be awesome. For most people, only a small portion of their tasks would have true deadlines. The current date property could be used to indicate when the user plans to complete the task. The new “deadline” property would represent when they need to complete it by, at the latest. To be able to filter tasks to see only ones with deadlines would be great.  To sort by deadline would be great too. Then you could reschedule your tasks in the calendar using the primary date property while still being able to keep track of their deadlines. 

Users could also view both when they plan to complete the task as well as when the task is due on the calendar. Those two dates would need to be visually differentiated of course, so users could tell them apart.

Some casual users might never understand the purpose of the extra “deadline” property, and that’s totally fine.

If this was done, TickTick would be a near perfect app.

title: this app is one of the best things in my life and i literally evangelize it to anyone and everyone
body:
i’ve been using tick tick for a few years now. important background info: i LOVE planning, i love categorizing, i love organization, i love note keeping and collecting and compiling information and media of all kinds. i love being able to customize and design any system i interact with to my needs and preferences as much possible. (i am an engineer and also autistic so when i say i love this stuff, i mean it. it’s a genuine passion and hobby for me) 

ticktick is fantastic for so many reasons, the fact that it’s cross platform is already just a huge huge plus. but i think ticktick’s design philosophy is what makes it so great. there are so SO many features, there are so many way to customize things, there are so many ways to tailor your tick tick exactly to your needs. if you want simplicity, you don’t have to deal with using extra complex features that you don’t need, especially since oftentimes complex or intricate functions and options are actually a hindrance for those who don’t need it. 

with tick tick, you can make your lists, notes, whatever, as simple as you want. you don’t need to deal with unnecessary complications if you don’t want them. nor do you have to deal with the visual clutter of features you don’t even use. this is a common issue i find on program and app design, where the excessive amount of options and buttons and features make them difficult to navigate and ultimately i will stop using them. and i love that tick tick puts so much work and effort into providing a wealth of options for customization ad well as options to interlink various notes, tags, media, you name it. but they also understand that is not what everyone needs, and they make it so so accessible and easy to just make simple lists without extra hassle or having some useless premium feature shoved in your face every time you open the app. 

for someone like me, i use basically all of the functions and features, i have created a wiki of sorts for various notes, i even use the link feature to link to notes in my native notes app! i love that you can create note folders/lists. its perfect for me as I can keep EVERYTHING i need in one place. 

i have a list that’s just full of resources and user guides for my electronics/tools and other things i reference a lot. it’s so amszingly helpful. I have a note list that contains helpful keyboard shortcut cheat sheets for various apps, and tick ticks sticky note feature allows me to pin those to the screen when i need them! i have a note list for shopping and wishlists, projects i want to do in the future.

i even have a list of notes ABOUT tick tick (because i am not normal about this obviously lol) including an in progress visual user guide im working on for my friends because i want to convert them, a note of various features i think would be great additions, user feedback, a list of things to add to my tick tick. 

i could give so many more examples of the amazing ways you can use this app to make it perfect for what you need, but i genuinely doubt anyone is still reading this far haha. 

as i said at the bringing of this novel of a review, lists and organizing and planning is a hobby and passion to me. if i get to spend a weekend entirely making and arrange lists, information, and spend time and energy to do it efficiently, affectively, accessibly, with optimized and streamlined design and of course above all, approachable, usable, easy to understand, and something that i can actually keep up with. balancing simplicity and readability with my love for automation, detailed descriptions and breakdowns of tasks, as well as notes and information i find relevant. i will be on cloud nine having the time of my life and then show off my work to my lowed ones who are very patient with me haha. 

so you can TRUST ME when I say this is an AMAZING app, i love it, and i know what im talking about ;p it’s the best one ive used and trust me i have used a lot lol. 

i will say that tick tick seems to be optimized and made for primarily people using it on their phone (which makes sense, it’s an app haha) and while the cross platform ability is so helpful, i find that the desktop version of the app (specifically the mac version) doesn’t receive updates as frequently, and i believe is missing features that are available on the phone app. 

also, the aesthetic customization on the desktop is both tedious and difficult to use for custom backgrounds, as the ability to preview and estimate the photo sizes to use and how they will actually look when applied makes it a long process for me. additionally (last i checked) the mac version doesn’t have the font customization features available
on windows :( it also doesn’t allow you to alter the text/font of “pinned” lists/folders. meaning that if the title of the pinned note is too long, it just gets cut off. i would even just like the ability to turn off the title text beneath the pins and just use the emojis for them so i don’t have to deal with the cut off titles. 

it would also be great to have a little more freedom in the custom theme options like picking your accent color and maybe some control over the actual text in the app, as it’s difficult to use a custom image and find a balance of opacity/blur/brightness that will make the text readable. which often means the photo you wanted as your background has to be very purposely sized and strategically placed, and usually ends up being far more cut off or distored/blurred than what you wanted in order to accommodate text visibility, since as i recall, you don’t get to pick the color of the text or like if it’s light mode/dark mode or whatever. 

all that being said, i am very neurotic and also love making things cute so im pretty sure no other person would care about all that. 

anyways perfect app, and if you’ve read all the way to the end of this, genuinely thank you lmao

title: Exceptional Work!
body:
Honestly, TickTick stands shoulder to shoulder with the best productivity apps out there. It handles continuity, syncing, and day to day task management extremely well. As a core to-do list manager, it really shines.

But no app nails every single category, and TickTick has a couple spots where it could level up. The Pomodoro feature is the main one. It doesn’t really need its own bottom tab just to show a single “Start” button. That space could be used for something more functional. The timer would make more sense sitting inside the “Home” tab, right next to your tasks, so it naturally supports the list you’re actually working on. A Pomodoro should feel integrated, not separate.

The Habit Tracker could also benefit from duration tracking. If I plan to read for 15 minutes but end up reading for 25 minutes, that extra effort should be reflected. And yes, there’s the Pomodoro timer, but it doesn’t fully connect to either habits or tasks, so the ecosystem never quite syncs together the way you’d hope.

And clearing out bad habits could definitely be more intuitive and front and center.

All that said, TickTick is still an excellent app. For what it offers, it provides exceptional value, and the overall experience is hard to beat. With a few thoughtful adjustments, it could easily become the gold standard for productivity apps.

title: Amazing productivity and task managing app
body:
This is quite simply one of the absolute best to do list and overall productivity apps I have ever used in my 16 years as an iPhone user.

First and foremost, it allows you to pick which functions you need and which you don’t: calendar, Eisenhower matrix, habit tracker, pomodoro timer, etc.

Then, the Eisenhower matrix function alone is more powerful and allows for more color-coding, categorization and reminder settings – even in just the free tier – than some dedicated matrix apps (i.e. Focus Matrix, Priority Matrix).

The habit tracker function alone is essentially the entire “Productive - Habit Tracker” (app as it was in 2017) crammed into a single tab on this app.

I am impressed and blown away and plan to continue using this app many years into the future, even despite already having and using Focus Bean, Proton Calendar, outset, and of course, the basic iOS apps. 

Here’s to many more years of insanely powerful and thorough project/habit/task tracking & management.

title: life-changer

When I downloaded it in another effort to finally find the right system for me, I was immediately impressed with the inclusion of a built-in Eisenhower matrix system- something I used to do on paper all the time to try and prioritize my work. As I’ve continued using it for the last year or so, I’ve only become even happier with it. Finally, something that has all of the features I want, that work in a way that makes sense. I can’t thank the developers enough!
